title: White House Divided Over Chinese AI as Startups Warn Ban Would Kill Innovation
excerpt: Nearly 200 U.S. startups pushed back against proposed restrictions on Chinese AI models as the Trump administration accused Moonshot AI of stealing Anthropic's technology.
body:
• Nearly 200 U.S. startups urged the Trump administration against banning Chinese open-weight AI models, warning such a move would destroy hundreds of companies that rely on affordable alternatives to costly American systems.
  • The White House accused Beijing's Moonshot AI of stealing Anthropic's proprietary technology through "large-scale, covert distillation" to build its Kimi K3 model, which rivals top U.S. AI systems.
  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned of potential sanctions against Chinese AI labs, while White House AI adviser David Sacks argued restrictions would benefit only a handful of dominant U.S. labs at the expense of innovation.
  • Kimi K3's open weights release on July 27 will test Washington's enforcement capacity — once model files spread globally, restrictions become nearly impossible to apply.

A sharp divide has opened inside the Trump administration over how to handle the rapid rise of Chinese AI models that American companies increasingly depend on — and that Washington suspects were built on stolen technology.

The clash came into full view this week as nearly 200 Silicon Valley startups, organized under the newly formed Little Tech Association, sent letters to President Trump, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and other senior officials urging against a blanket ban on Chinese open-weight AI models, according to Politico.

The Kimi K3 Trigger

The debate intensified after Moonshot AI, a Beijing-based startup, released Kimi K3 — a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that topped front-end coding leaderboards and matched or exceeded Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol on several benchmarks. The model activates only 16 of its 896 experts per token, delivering frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost. Full open weights are scheduled for release on July 27.

Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, accused Moonshot AI of building "a sophisticated internal platform to conduct large-scale distillation against U.S. models, allowing them to quickly switch between multiple methods of access to avoid detection." He also alleged the firm acquired banned Nvidia GB300 servers.

"There's a very technical AI word for it called distillation, but you and I would call it theft."

— Scott Bessent, U.S. Treasury Secretary, on Fox Business

Startups Sound the Alarm

"There'll be hundreds of companies that instantly die," Suhail Doshi, founder of AI infrastructure startup Particle, told reporters. "It's great for Anthropic. We're all going to have to spend money on Anthropic."

The economics driving adoption are stark. DeepSeek-V4-Pro delivers output for 87 cents per million tokens, according to WebProNews. Anthropic's Claude costs $50 for the same volume. Coinbase has slashed its AI spending nearly in half by switching to Chinese alternatives. Shopify, Airbnb, and other major firms have integrated Alibaba's Qwen models into their operations.

Harry Godfrey, executive director of the Little Tech Association, called for "a scalpel rather than a sledgehammer" — targeted safeguards against genuine intellectual property theft without broad bans that would raise costs for American builders.

The Administration's Internal Split

David Sacks, AI investor and White House tech adviser, has publicly pushed back against restrictions. "The leading closed labs, already a duopoly in terms of AI model revenue, want the government to eliminate their open-source competition," Sacks wrote on X. He argued the U.S. risks tying itself in knots with data-center restrictions and pre-approval rules while Chinese models advance unchecked.

On the other side, Treasury Secretary Bessent pointed to detected watermarks from U.S. large language models embedded in Chinese counterparts as evidence of theft. Anthropic's head of public policy, Sarah Heck, called covert distillation "IP theft and industrial espionage that supports adversary military and intelligence capabilities."

Congressional committees have also launched reviews. House Homeland Security Committee Chairman Andrew Garbarino and House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar announced a joint investigation into Chinese open-source models using distillation to boost their capabilities via American AI systems.

Why Indian Tech Should Watch

The outcome carries direct consequences for India's technology sector. Indian startups and IT services firms that have adopted Chinese open-weight models for cost-effective AI deployment could face disruption if Washington imposes broad restrictions. India's own AI ambitions, including government-backed initiatives for sovereign AI models, may also be shaped by how the U.S. draws the line between open innovation and national security.

The July 27 weight release will force the administration's hand. Once model files circulate globally, enforcement becomes largely symbolic. As analysts at the Peterson Institute for International Economics have cautioned, ad hoc controls could accelerate international adoption of Chinese models precisely because downloaded weights cannot be revoked.
nri_angle: Indian startups and IT services firms relying on cost-effective Chinese open-weight AI models could face disruption if Washington imposes broad restrictions, with implications for India's own sovereign AI ambitions.
